title: Walter Payton's birth chart
metaDescription: Walter Payton's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 2.2° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 2.2° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Leo, but precisely: 2.2°, first decan, 0°–10°, under the Sun in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 12.6° Cancer; Venus stands at 14.1° Virgo; Mars stands at 25.7° Sagittarius. The tradition reads a mind that absorbs before it argues from Mercury, taste for the substantial and the lasting from Venus, drive that ignites on contact from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Venus and Jupiter — a sextile holding at 0.1°. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, Uranus square Neptune at 0.5°, and Neptune sextile Pluto at 0.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. The Sun in Leo at 2.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Venus in Virgo at 14.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Cancer at 14.0° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 water, 3 fire, 2 air, 1 earth; by modality, 4 cardinal, 3 fixed, 3 mutable. Water signs hold memory in the scheme, where nothing is quite finished and little is genuinely forgotten. Mars was retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.1° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 8.0°.
